# Provisional HCC hypothesis (early draft)

## Proposed relationship
Among adults with a documented liver cancer diagnosis in this HCC hospital dataset, the presence of a recorded major liver-directed treatment during the early post-diagnosis interval is associated with lower 1-year all-cause mortality than no recorded treatment, after accounting for baseline age, sex, comorbidity burden, and documented disease stage when available.

This is an observational prognostic/treatment-association hypothesis, not a causal claim. The key unresolved question is whether the apparent survival advantage reflects treatment benefit or is explained by healthier treated patients, stage/extent of disease, access and documentation intensity, or informative loss to follow-up.

## Grounding and evidence limits
The dataset card confirms that HCC contains read-only encounter, diagnosis, laboratory, examination, medication, procedure, pathology, clinical-document and vital-sign tables, with exact source files and table schemas under `datasets/hcc/`. The diagnosis table can define the index liver-cancer population; procedure and medication tables can identify liver-directed interventions; encounter and diagnosis fields can support baseline covariates and follow-up. I have not yet inspected row-level values or verified treatment-code coverage, stage completeness, or mortality ascertainment, so no effect estimate or clinical conclusion is claimed here.

## Falsifiable test
Define an index date from the first qualifying liver-cancer diagnosis. Compare patients with and without a recorded liver-directed procedure/medication in a prespecified early window (for example, 0–30 days), with 1-year mortality as the primary outcome. Use patient-level time-zero covariates only, censor at discharge/last documented contact or loss to follow-up, and report standardized mortality risk differences with confidence intervals. A prespecified negative-control or timing analysis (treatment recorded after index but before the outcome window) and sensitivity analyses excluding undocumented stage or short-stay patients will test selection and documentation explanations.

Supportive result: a reproducible adjusted survival difference with plausible timing and robustness to missingness. Adverse result: no difference, reversal, or dependence on treatment selection/documentation proxies. Inconclusive result: wide intervals, sparse treatment, poor stage coverage, or non-identifiable follow-up. None of these outcomes establishes causality without clinical adjudication and stronger treatment-assignment evidence.

## Required next checks
Inspect exact HCC table columns and source headers; verify index-date and patient keys; quantify treatment, stage, and mortality coverage; choose a defensible treatment definition; and bind the final experiment to exact files, joins, and time fields. The final proposal must also include three inspected key works with frozen receipts; none are asserted in this provisional draft.

# Provisional hypothesis: discordant renal recovery after acute kidney injury

## Proposed relationship
Among adults with an acute kidney injury (AKI) episode in MIMIC-IV, patients whose creatinine has returned toward baseline but whose urine output and/or fluid balance remain abnormal at a prespecified 48-hour assessment will have a higher risk of subsequent in-hospital death or persistent/recurrent kidney dysfunction than patients with concordant creatinine and urine-output recovery, after accounting for baseline illness severity and treatment context.

This is a hypothesis, not an observed result. The clinical opening is that creatinine-based recovery may be a misleading surrogate: creatinine can fall because of dilution, altered production, or recovery while residual tubular dysfunction or fluid overload persists. Resolving this would clarify whether a single creatinine criterion is sufficient for judging renal recovery and for deciding whether continued monitoring or renal-risk assessment is warranted.

## Concrete supporting observations and source locations
- The expert seed `expert-20260913-mimic-03` (candidate `candidate-209a992a877034bf9d300fd7`) explicitly proposes that creatinine falling without improvement in urine output or fluid status leaves patients at high risk, and identifies the limitation that measured kidney function is unavailable.
- The seed points to the comparison of cystatin C and creatinine during critical illness (PMID 37256861) as a measurement reference; this supports the premise that creatinine alone may not represent kidney function, but it does not establish the proposed outcome association.
- The MIMIC-IV dataset is the assigned source and is expected to contain longitudinal laboratory, urine-output, fluid-balance, vital-sign, medication, and outcome data; exact table/column bindings still require catalog inspection before the final experiment card.

## Uncertainties and missing evidence
- AKI onset, baseline creatinine, recovery timing, and “persistent urine-output/fluid abnormality” must be operationalized without future information.
- Creatinine and urine output are imperfect and selectively measured; fluid balance is affected by treatment and documentation.
- The available data may not contain measured GFR, cystatin C, dialysis details sufficient for adjudication, or reliable reasons for discharge/ICU transfer.
- Severity, nephrotoxic drugs, vasopressors, diuretics, dialysis, and fluid management can confound or mediate the association; a retrospective design cannot by itself identify a causal mechanism.
- The literature claim and exact MIMIC tables/columns have not yet been fully inspected in this provisional checkpoint.

## Falsifiable test
Use a fixed landmark at 48 hours after an operational AKI onset (or the first qualifying AKI assessment), with outcomes assessed only after that landmark: in-hospital death and a prespecified persistent/recurrent kidney endpoint. Compare discordant recovery with concordant recovery using a prespecified multivariable baseline/landmark model and a competing-risk or time-to-event analysis. Report effect estimates and uncertainty, calibration, and sensitivity analyses for missingness, treatment, and alternative AKI definitions.

Support would be a reproducible adjusted association with clinically meaningful uncertainty and robustness to measurement/timing sensitivity analyses. Adverse evidence would be no association, reversal, or instability under prespecified sensitivity analyses, arguing against using this discordance as a risk marker. Inconclusive evidence would be insufficient event support, excessive missingness, or wide intervals that cannot distinguish a clinically important effect.

## Required next evidence
Inspect the complete MIMIC catalog and relevant table schemas; acquire and read the cited measurement work plus two additional closest works; define exact joins, time fields, cohort filters, and outcome windows; and compare a simple landmark baseline with a substantive longitudinal learned or mechanistic alternative before selecting the final method.

# HCC early liver-directed treatment and 1-year mortality: working proposal

## Scientific opening and unresolved question
The configured HCC data contain many patients with liver-cancer diagnoses and repeated encounters, procedures, medications, examinations, and clinical documents. A recorded liver-directed intervention may be associated with survival, but the clinically important uncertainty is whether that association reflects treatment benefit or competing explanations: patients selected for treatment may have different tumor burden/stage, liver reserve, performance status, access, or documentation intensity; and survival follow-up may be incomplete or informative.

The provisional hypothesis is: among adults with a first documented HCC diagnosis in the HCC dataset, receiving a recorded liver-directed treatment during the early post-index interval is associated with lower 1-year all-cause mortality than no recorded treatment, after adjustment for baseline age, sex, comorbidity burden, disease stage/extent when documented, and treatment-selection proxies. This is an observational treatment-association hypothesis, not a causal treatment-benefit claim.

The leading rival explanations are (1) stage and tumor burden: earlier or less extensive disease is more likely to receive treatment and has better prognosis; (2) selection/healthcare access: treatment receipt reflects availability, performance status, and clinician judgment; (3) documentation intensity: more observed encounters produce more recorded procedures and more complete follow-up; and (4) informative censoring: patients with sparse follow-up may appear to survive or die differently. A treatment association that disappears after stage/selection adjustment, or is concentrated among patients with dense documentation, supports a rival explanation rather than treatment benefit.

## Exact dataset bindings and verified availability
The catalog `datasets/README.md`/`catalog.json` identifies the HCC snapshot and read-only CSV sources. The relevant tables and exact columns are:

- `diagnoses` from `[private-path]/data_诊断_7504718184492840569.csv`: `患者主索引`, `就诊号`, `诊断名称`, `诊断类型`. Header and rows were inspected. It contains 1,810,646 diagnosis rows, 43,815 patients, and 105,044 visit keys; common HCC labels include `肝细胞癌` (336,570 rows), `肝恶性肿瘤` (48,212), and stage-bearing labels such as `肝细胞癌(CNLC Ia)`.
- `encounters` from `[private-path]/data_基本信息_2500296761891079109.csv`: `患者主索引`, `就诊号`, `姓名`, `身份证号`, `手机号`, `医保/就诊卡号`, `住院号`, `年龄`, `性别`, `身高`, `体重`, `就诊时间`, `入院时间`, `出院时间`, `就诊科室`. Header and rows were inspected. It has 105,044 encounter rows and 43,815 patients; `就诊时间`, `入院时间`, and `出院时间` are the encounter time fields. Direct identifiers must not be used in outputs or public queries.
- `procedures` from `[private-path]/data_手术_8024330590283626027.csv`: `患者主索引`, `就诊号`, `手术`, `开始时间`, `结束时间`, `手术来源`. Header and rows were inspected. It has 338,040 procedure rows and 43,062 patients. Observed treatment labels include `TACE`, `经导管肝动脉栓塞术`, `动脉化疗栓塞`, `肝叶部分切除术`, `腹腔镜下肝部分切除术`, `超声引导下肝病损微波消融术`, and `超声引导下肝病损射频消融术`.
- `medications` from `[private-path]/data_用药_5693407050835159466.csv`: `患者主索引`, `就诊号`, `用药`, `单次用药计量`, `单次用药计量单位`, `频次`, `开始时间`, `结束时间`, `用药方式`, `药品类型`. Header and rows were inspected. It has 4,097,517 medication rows and 43,610 patients. It can support systemic therapy signals, but the primary treatment definition should be procedure-based because medication labels are heterogeneous and many are supportive infusions.
- `examinations` from `[private-path]/data_检查_4203595081195465282.csv`: `患者主索引`, `就诊号`, `检查`, `检查所见`, `检查诊断`, `开始时间`, `机器型号`, `检查号`. Header and rows were inspected. It can provide imaging burden/stage and documentation-density covariates; narrative text is available but not yet adjudicated.
- `labs` from `[private-path]/data_检验_609065997844652188.csv`: `患者主索引`, `就诊号`, `检验`, `定性结果`, `定量结果`, `标本类型`, `检验时间`. Header and rows were inspected. It can provide baseline liver function and tumor-marker covariates after a prespecified analytic mapping; no mapping has yet been validated.
- `clinical_documents` from `[private-path]/data_病历文书_8434587325530196878.csv`: `患者主索引`, `就诊号`, `主诉`, `现病史`, `既往史`, `个人史`, `月经史`, `婚育史`, `家族史`, `入院诊断`, `入院情况`, `入院诊断__duplicate_2`, `诊疗经过`, `出院情况`, `出院诊断`, `手术名称`, `手术经过`. Header and rows were inspected. It may improve stage, performance status, and treatment-intent adjudication, but text is not yet systematically parsed.
- `pathology` from `[private-path]/data_病理_3292603985559017792.csv`: `患者主索引`, `就诊号`, `病理`, `检查所见`, `检查诊断`, `机器型号`. Header and rows were inspected. It can support histologic confirmation when available, but is not guaranteed for every HCC case.
- `orders` from `[private-path]/data_医嘱(非药品)_2062526727266216118.csv`: `患者主索引`, `就诊号`, `医嘱(非药品)`, `开立时间`, `开始时间`, `结束时间`, `医嘱期限`, `医嘱状态`, `频次`. It can be used for documentation-density and planned-procedure checks, not as the primary treatment indicator.
- `vitals` (`data_体征数据_3824052911997097911.csv`) and `transfers` (`data_出入转_7369490831683459252.csv`) contain only `患者主索引`, `就诊号` in the catalog and are identifier-only, so they cannot supply vital values or transfer timing in this analysis.

All joins must use the documented HCC key pair `(患者主索引, 就诊号)` within HCC; no cross-dataset joins are proposed. Patient-level aggregation uses `患者主索引`, while encounter-level time alignment uses both keys.

## Index population and time zero
Construct the index cohort from the first qualifying HCC diagnosis for each `患者主索引`, using `diagnoses.诊断名称` and `diagnoses.诊断类型`, with a prespecified rule: include current/primary HCC labels such as `肝细胞癌` or `肝恶性肿瘤` and exclude explicit personal-history labels (`肝恶性肿瘤个人史`) and, in a sensitivity analysis, explicit postoperative/recurrent labels. Join the qualifying diagnosis to `encounters` on `(患者主索引, 就诊号)` and use the earliest `就诊时间` (with `入院时间` as a documented tie-breaker) as index time. Require a valid encounter row and index date. If the diagnosis table has no timestamp, the encounter time is the operational index time; this limitation must be reported.

Primary treatment definition: a procedure row in `procedures` with `开始时间` from index time through index time + 30 days and a prespecified liver-directed label set. The label set is to be frozen after a bounded review of the observed procedure vocabulary; initial candidates are TACE/embolization (`TACE`, `经导管肝动脉栓塞术`, `动脉化疗栓塞`, `经动脉造影化疗栓塞术（TACE）`), hepatic resection (`肝叶切除术`, `肝叶部分切除术`, `腹腔镜下肝部分切除术`, `部分肝切除术`, `特殊肝段切除术`), and ablation (`微波消融`, `射频消融`). `TACE` and its variants are not to be double-counted as separate modalities. A secondary definition adds systemic therapy from `medications` only after a prespecified drug-name mapping is reviewed; it is not mixed into the primary definition.

Patients with a qualifying procedure before index time are excluded from the primary incident-treatment cohort, with a sensitivity analysis retaining them and labeling prior treatment. Patients with no qualifying procedure through 30 days are the untreated comparator. Treatment is time-zero exposure, not a time-varying exposure, to avoid post-index outcome conditioning.

## Covariates, outcome, and follow-up
Baseline covariates are measured or derived from records dated at or before index time: age and sex from `encounters`; department from `encounters.就诊科室`; comorbidity indicators from pre-index `diagnoses`; liver disease indicators from pre-index diagnoses (`肝硬化`, `乙肝后肝硬化`, `门静脉高压`, `门静脉瘤栓`, etc.); baseline laboratory values from `labs` using the last valid result in a prespecified 30-day pre-index window, with missingness indicators; imaging/examination count and stage-related text features from `examinations`; and documentation density from the number of encounters, diagnoses, labs, examinations, and orders before index. Stage is a primary covariate only when extractable from diagnosis labels or adjudicated text; otherwise it is an uncertainty, not silently imputed as known.

The primary outcome is all-cause mortality within 365 days of index time. Because the catalog has no explicit death table, mortality must be operationalized as an in-hospital death outcome only if a death field is found and validated in the source rows; otherwise the primary outcome is unavailable and the study must not claim 1-year mortality. The fallback computable endpoint is 1-year observed survival/contact status using the last documented HCC encounter (`出院时间`/`就诊时间`) as administrative censoring, explicitly labeled as informative and not equivalent to mortality. A second analysis may use death recorded in clinical documents or diagnoses only after prespecified text adjudication; this requires expert review.

Follow-up is from index time to the earliest of 365 days, validated death, or last documented contact. Patients with no later encounter are censored at last contact, not assumed alive. Report the proportion with follow-up beyond 30, 90, and 365 days, and perform inverse-probability-of-censoring sensitivity analysis. The key limitation is that this dataset may not contain reliable external mortality capture; any mortality conclusion is conditional on the operational endpoint and must state that limitation.

## Baseline and substantive alternative
The simple baseline is a prespecified cause-specific or fine-Gray model for the operational 1-year endpoint, with treatment as the exposure and a transparent adjustment set: age, sex, index department, comorbidity/liver-disease indicators, documented stage, baseline laboratory values, and documentation density. Report standardized mortality/contact risk differences and 95% confidence intervals, with missing-stage and missing-lab sensitivity analyses. This baseline tests the adjusted association but loses nonlinear interactions, time-varying observation processes, and the distinction between treatment assignment and treatment effect.

The substantive alternative is a two-part selection/observation model: (i) estimate treatment propensity from baseline covariates and documentation intensity, and (ii) estimate the outcome and censoring models, then compare standardized risks under the treated and untreated exposure distributions using inverse-probability weighting or g-computation, with overlap diagnostics and a prespecified positivity threshold. A secondary learned model (gradient-boosted survival model or regularized cause-specific model) can use the same baseline inputs and predict the endpoint, but it is evaluated for calibration, discrimination, and treatment-effect stability—not rewarded for a small predictive gain. The alternative reveals whether the association is concentrated in a selected treatment region, whether documentation intensity explains it, and whether nonlinear stage/liver-reserve interactions change the adjusted estimate. It does not identify a causal mechanism.

Both methods use the same patient-level split (e.g., 70/30 by `患者主索引`, with no patient appearing in both train and test), the same endpoint, and the same uncertainty evaluation (bootstrap or cluster-robust confidence intervals; calibration plots; standardized risk differences). The baseline is selected as the primary interpretable analysis; the learned/selection model is retained because it tests the clinically important selection and documentation rivals. A GPU is not required for these tabular analyses; CPU is adequate unless the learned model is expanded, in which case a bounded allocated probe should verify runtime.

## Falsification and interpretation
Pre-specify these checks before fitting: (1) treatment labels recorded after index but before the 30-day window are excluded from exposure and used as a timing/negative-control check; (2) a pseudo-treatment date shifted outside the early window should not reproduce the association; (3) exclude patients with no post-index contact and compare with censoring-weighted results; (4) stratify by documented stage and documentation density; (5) compare procedure-only and procedure-plus-medication definitions; (6) assess positivity, missingness, and calibration. A supportive result requires a reproducible adjusted risk difference with adequate overlap and robustness to stage/missingness and censoring checks. An adverse result is no association, reversal, or disappearance after stage/documentation adjustment, which supports selection or documentation explanations. An inconclusive result is sparse treatment, poor stage coverage, inadequate follow-up, or wide intervals; it does not refute benefit.

No result from these observational analyses establishes that treatment causes survival benefit. Establishing causal benefit would require a validated mortality registry, reliable treatment assignment/intent, clinical adjudication of stage and performance status, and preferably a prospective or quasi-experimental design. The actual deliverable is a newly fitted, uncertainty-quantified treatment-association analysis with exact cohort construction, endpoint limitations, and rival-explanation diagnostics.

## Evidence status and next steps
The dataset headers and representative rows were inspected, and the diagnosis/procedure vocabulary was scanned. The key remaining checks are: validate whether any death/mortality field exists in the HCC source rows; freeze the procedure label map and stage extraction; quantify index-cohort size, treatment coverage, follow-up, and missingness; and inspect three hypothesis-specific public works with frozen receipts. No effect estimate or clinical conclusion is claimed yet.

Header and rows were inspected. It has 105,044 encounter rows and 43,815 patients; `就诊时间`, `入院时间`, and `出院时间` are the encounter time fields. Direct identifiers must not be used in outputs or public queries.
- `procedures` from `[private-path]/data_手术_8024330590283626027.csv`: `患者主索引`, `就诊号`, `手术`, `开始时间`, `结束时间`, `手术来源`. Header and rows were inspected. It has 338,040 procedure rows and 43,062 patients. Observed treatment labels include `TACE`, `经导管肝动脉栓塞术`, `动脉化疗栓塞`, `肝叶部分切除术`, `腹腔镜下肝部分切除术`, `超声引导下肝病损微波消融术`, and `超声引导下肝病损射频消融术`.
- `medications` from `[private-path]/data_用药_5693407050835159466.csv`: `患者主索引`, `就诊号`, `用药`, `单次用药计量`, `单次用药计量单位`, `频次`, `开始时间`, `结束时间`, `用药方式`, `药品类型`. Header and rows were inspected. It has 4,097,517 medication rows and 43,610 patients. It can support systemic therapy signals, but the primary treatment definition should be procedure-based because medication labels are heterogeneous and many are supportive infusions.
- `examinations` from `[private-path]/data_检查_4203595081195465282.csv`: `患者主索引`, `就诊号`, `检查`, `检查所见`, `检查诊断`, `开始时间`, `机器型号`, `检查号`. Header and rows were inspected. It can provide imaging burden/stage and documentation-density covariates; narrative text is available but not yet adjudicated.
- `labs` from `[private-path]/data_检验_609065997844652188.csv`: `患者主索引`, `就诊号`, `检验`, `定性结果`, `定量结果`, `标本类型`, `检验时间`. Header and rows were inspected. It can provide baseline liver function and tumor-marker covariates after a prespecified analytic mapping; no mapping has yet been validated.
- `clinical_documents` from `[private-path]/data_病历文书_8434587325530196878.csv`: `患者主索引`, `就诊号`, `主诉`, `现病史`, `既往史`, `个人史`, `月经史`, `婚育史`, `家族史`, `入院诊断`, `入院情况`, `入院诊断__duplicate_2`, `诊疗经过`, `出院情况`, `出院诊断`, `手术名称`, `手术经过`. Header and rows were inspected. It may improve stage, performance status, and treatment-intent adjudication, but text is not yet systematically parsed.
- `pathology` from `[private-path]/data_病理_3292603985559017792.csv`: `患者主索引`, `就诊号`, `病理`, `检查所见`, `检查诊断`, `机器型号`. Header and rows were inspected. It can support histologic confirmation when available, but is not guaranteed for every HCC case.
- `orders` from `[private-path]/data_医嘱(非药品)_2062526727266216118.csv`: `患者主索引`, `就诊号`, `医嘱(非药品)`, `开立时间`, `开始时间`, `结束时间`, `医嘱期限`, `医嘱状态`, `频次`. It can be used for documentation-density and planned-procedure checks, not as the primary treatment indicator.
- `vitals` (`data_体征数据_3824052911997097911.csv`) and `transfers` (`data_出入转_7369490831683459252.csv`) contain only `患者主索引`, `就诊号` in the catalog and are identifier-only, so they cannot supply vital values or transfer timing in this analysis.

All joins must use the documented HCC key pair `(患者主索引, 就诊号)` within HCC; no cross-dataset joins are proposed. Patient-level aggregation uses `患者主索引`, while encounter-level time alignment uses both keys.

## Index population and time zero
Construct the index cohort from the first qualifying HCC diagnosis for each `患者主索引`, using `diagnoses.诊断名称` and `diagnoses.诊断类型`, with a prespecified rule: include current/primary HCC labels such as `肝细胞癌` or `肝恶性肿瘤` and exclude explicit personal-history labels (`肝恶性肿瘤个人史`) and, in a sensitivity analysis, explicit postoperative/recurrent labels. Join the qualifying diagnosis to `encounters` on `(患者主索引, 就诊号)` and use the earliest `就诊时间` (with `入院时间` as a documented tie-breaker) as index time. Require a valid encounter row and index date. If the diagnosis table has no timestamp, the encounter time is the operational index time; this limitation must be reported.

Primary treatment definition: a procedure row in `procedures` with `开始时间` from index time through index time + 30 days and a prespecified liver-directed label set. The label set is to be frozen after a bounded review of the observed procedure vocabulary; initial candidates are TACE/embolization (`TACE`, `经导管肝动脉栓塞术`, `动脉化疗栓塞`, `经动脉造影化疗栓塞术（TACE）`), hepatic resection (`肝叶切除术`, `肝叶部分切除术`, `腹腔镜下肝部分切除术`, `部分肝切除术`, `特殊肝段切除术`), and ablation (`微波消融`, `射频消融`). `TACE` and its variants are not to be double-counted as separate modalities. A secondary definition adds systemic therapy from `medications` only after a prespecified drug-name mapping is reviewed; it is not mixed into the primary definition.

Patients with a qualifying procedure before index time are excluded from the primary incident-treatment cohort, with a sensitivity analysis retaining them and labeling prior treatment. Patients with no qualifying procedure through 30 days are the untreated comparator. Treatment is time-zero exposure, not a time-varying exposure, to avoid post-index outcome conditioning.

## Covariates, outcome, and follow-up
Baseline covariates are measured or derived from records dated at or before index time: age and sex from `encounters`; department from `encounters.就诊科室`; comorbidity indicators from pre-index `diagnoses`; liver disease indicators from pre-index diagnoses (`肝硬化`, `乙肝后肝硬化`, `门静脉高压`, `门静脉瘤栓`, etc.); baseline laboratory values from `labs` using the last valid result in a prespecified 30-day pre-index window, with missingness indicators; imaging/examination count and stage-related text features from `examinations`; and documentation density from the number of encounters, diagnoses, labs, examinations, and orders before index. Stage is a primary covariate only when extractable from diagnosis labels or adjudicated text; otherwise it is an uncertainty, not silently imputed as known.

The primary outcome is all-cause mortality within 365 days of index time. Because the catalog has no explicit death table, mortality must be operationalized as an in-hospital death outcome only if a death field is found and validated in the source rows; otherwise the primary outcome is unavailable and the study must not claim 1-year mortality. The fallback computable endpoint is 1-year observed survival/contact status using the last documented HCC encounter (`出院时间`/`就诊时间`) as administrative censoring, explicitly labeled as informative and not equivalent to mortality. A second analysis may use death recorded in clinical documents or diagnoses only after prespecified text adjudication; this requires expert review.

Follow-up is from index time to the earliest of 365 days, validated death, or last documented contact. Patients with no later encounter are censored at last contact, not assumed alive. Report the proportion with follow-up beyond 30, 90, and 365 days, and perform inverse-probability-of-censoring sensitivity analysis. The key limitation is that this dataset may not contain reliable external mortality capture; any mortality conclusion is conditional on the operational endpoint and must state that limitation.

## Baseline and substantive alternative
The simple baseline is a prespecified cause-specific or fine-Gray model for the operational 1-year endpoint, with treatment as the exposure and a transparent adjustment set: age, sex, index department, comorbidity/liver-disease indicators, documented stage, baseline laboratory values, and documentation density. Report standardized mortality/contact risk differences and 95% confidence intervals, with missing-stage and missing-lab sensitivity analyses. This baseline tests the adjusted association but loses nonlinear interactions, time-varying observation processes, and the distinction between treatment assignment and treatment effect.

The substantive alternative is a two-part selection/observation model: (i) estimate treatment propensity from baseline covariates and documentation intensity, and (ii) estimate the outcome and censoring models, then compare standardized risks under the treated and untreated exposure distributions using inverse-probability weighting or g-computation, with overlap diagnostics and a prespecified positivity threshold. A secondary learned model (gradient-boosted survival model or regularized cause-specific model) can use the same baseline inputs and predict the endpoint, but it is evaluated for calibration, discrimination, and treatment-effect stability—not rewarded for a small predictive gain. The alternative reveals whether the association is concentrated in a selected treatment region, whether documentation intensity explains it, and whether nonlinear stage/liver-reserve interactions change the adjusted estimate. It does not identify a causal mechanism.

Both methods use the same patient-level split (e.g., 70/30 by `患者主索引`, with no patient appearing in both train and test), the same endpoint, and the same uncertainty evaluation (bootstrap or cluster-robust confidence intervals; calibration plots; standardized risk differences). The baseline is selected as the primary interpretable analysis; the learned/selection model is retained because it tests the clinically important selection and documentation rivals. A GPU is not required for these tabular analyses; CPU is adequate unless the learned model is expanded, in which case a bounded allocated probe should verify runtime.

## Falsification and interpretation
Pre-specify these checks before fitting: (1) treatment labels recorded after index but before the 30-day window are excluded from exposure and used as a timing/negative-control check; (2) a pseudo-treatment date shifted outside the early window should not reproduce the association; (3) exclude patients with no post-index contact and compare with censoring-weighted results; (4) stratify by documented stage and documentation density; (5) compare procedure-only and procedure-plus-medication definitions; (6) assess positivity, missingness, and calibration. A supportive result requires a reproducible adjusted risk difference with adequate overlap and robustness to stage/missingness and censoring checks. An adverse result is no association, reversal, or disappearance after stage/documentation adjustment, which supports selection or documentation explanations. An inconclusive result is sparse treatment, poor stage coverage, inadequate follow-up, or wide intervals; it does not refute benefit.

No result from these observational analyses establishes that treatment causes survival benefit. Establishing causal benefit would require a validated mortality registry, reliable treatment assignment/intent, clinical adjudication of stage and performance status, and preferably a prospective or quasi-experimental design. The actual deliverable is a newly fitted, uncertainty-quantified treatment-association analysis with exact cohort construction, endpoint limitations, and rival-explanation diagnostics.

## Evidence status and next steps
The dataset headers and representative rows were inspected, and the diagnosis/procedure vocabulary was scanned. The key remaining checks are: validate whether any death/mortality field exists in the HCC source rows; freeze the procedure label map and stage extraction; quantify index-cohort size, treatment coverage, follow-up, and missingness; and inspect three hypothesis-specific public works with frozen receipts. No effect estimate or clinical conclusion is claimed yet.
